key_insight: For physics-informed PDE solvers, discretization-based constraints increasingly outperform automatic differentiation as PDE nonlinearity and discontinuity grow, especially in harder boundary-condition settings.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical rule for choosing neural PDE solvers in engineering: use discretization-based constraints and often GNNs when robustness on complex, high-Mach, or strongly nonlinear flows matters most.
method: Compared AD-based PINNs against discretization-based constraints across a range of PDE difficulty, from Poisson to hypersonic flows.
Decomposed performance into approximation, optimization, and truncation errors to identify what limits each approach.
Compared two network backbones, MLP and GNN, under different nonlinearity and boundary-condition regimes.
evidence_signal: The paper reports systematic experiments over problems ranging from linear Poisson to high-Mach hypersonic flows, using source data and code to support the evaluation.
watch_item: Discretization-based methods can gain accuracy in difficult regimes, but their truncation error and problem-specific discretization choices must be managed carefully.
paper_title: A Systematic Analysis of Automatic Differentiation versus Discretization-based Constraints for Physics-Informed PDE Solvers
